design_reference: Editeur Livre-Jeu - Wireframes.dc.html § 02 « Éditeur — vue d'ensemble de l'arbre » (BINDING): top bar with book title + node count + « + Nœud »; dot-grid canvas; node cards with NodeBadge + ref + title + 1-line snippet; SVG connectors with arrowheads + mono edge labels; dashed-curve « fuite » relink edge; bottom-right zoom controls. Node marks from foundations/badges-nodes.html; cards/badges/tokens from styles.css. Low-fi, light theme.

plan.goal: Render the book as a navigable graph of node cards and labelled edges on a dot-grid canvas, with selection, pan/zoom, and the entry point to add a node — the primary editor surface.
acceptance_criteria: The canvas renders one card per node and one edge per relationship, read live from BookService; adding/removing/renaming a node or edge elsewhere updates the canvas without reload (driven by node:* / edge:* events).
Each node card shows its type via the correct NodeBadge mark, its ref, its title, and a 1-line snippet of its description.
Clicking a node selects it (accent border + ring) and emits node:selected{nodeId}; exactly one node is selected at a time; clicking empty canvas clears selection.
`choice` edges render solid and `relink`/`flee` edges render dashed; every edge shows its choice-label chip; the obligatory Mort node is reachable only via authored edges.
The canvas pans (drag) and zooms (controls + wheel); pan/zoom and the canvas↔outline view mode persist per book via UIPreferencesService and are NOT pushed to cloud sync.
« + Nœud » creates a new unattached node through BookService and selects it; the seeded empty book still shows Sommaire + Mort with an inviting affordance to author the first leaf.

The canvas auto-lays-out the book as a top-down tree (sommaire at the top; each node's direct children on one evenly-spaced row beneath it, parent centred over them, recursively; downward links). Linkless nodes (the isolated mort, any page not reached from the sommaire by a choice edge) wrap into a grid below the tree — never a single horizontal row nor a single descending column. Deterministic and stable across reloads, never overlapping at 0,0. Manual drag + per-book position persistence is a later iteration (a stored position will then override the computed slot).
Selecting a node here is what opens node-editor's side panel (via node:selected) — the canvas owns selection, not editing.
All chrome renders from design-system tokens/components, light theme; node cards stay legible at default zoom (title ≥ --fs-body).
plan.walking_skeleton: Read the open book from BookService, lay nodes out (stored position or auto-layout), draw cards + SVG edges on a dot-grid. Click a card → emit node:selected. Wire node:*/edge:* listeners to re-render. A faithful static graph with live selection.

iterations.goal: Faithful static render of § 02: cards with correct NodeBadge marks, refs, titles, snippets; solid/dashed SVG edges with arrowheads and centered label chips; top bar; zoom controls. DS fidelity pass.

Live data binding: render from BookService; subscribe to node:* / edge:* to update incrementally; « + Nœud » creates+selects a node; selection emits node:selected and is single-select with clear-on-empty-click.

Pan/zoom + layout persistence: drag-pan, wheel/control zoom (local, shipped), deterministic auto-layout for position-less nodes (shipped); PERSIST positions on drag + per-book view state via UIPreferencesService (not cloud-synced, KR-022) — deferred until UIPreferencesService lands.

Robustness at scale: virtualize / cull off-screen nodes for large books, avoid edge-label overlap, keep 60fps pan; guard against orphaned edges referencing deleted nodes (KR-021, partially shipped: orphans are dropped).

known_risks: KR-020 — The canvas is a VIEW, not the model: never mutate node/edge data locally; all changes go through BookService.
KR-021 — Orphaned edges must be dropped or visibly flagged, never rendered as a line to nowhere or a crash. Reconciled on every render via resolveEdges.
KR-022 — Pan/zoom and view-mode are UI preferences (UIPreferencesService), NOT part of the synced book document.

KR-023 — The canvas auto-lays-out the book as a top-down TREE (resolvePositions, a pure VIEW over the choice-edge structure): y by depth (each level a row beneath the previous), x by a leaf cursor with each parent centred over its children — sommaire at the top, direct children on one evenly-spaced row beneath, recursively. Linkless/unreachable nodes (the isolated mort, any page not reached by a choice edge) wrap into a GRID below the tree — never a single horizontal row ('all nodes horizontal') nor a single descending column ('one branch'); a wrapping grid avoids both. Deterministic, stable, no 0,0 pileup. Stored node.position is currently ignored by the view; manual drag + persistence is a later iteration.
KR-024 — Selection is owned here and broadcast via node:selected; node-editor must not own a competing selection source.

KR-025 — Per-device view state (pan/zoom, view-mode, dragged positions) lives in the brain UIPreferencesService over the RAW local store (never the sync decorator, KR-022/093); dragged positions are a UI preference (not synced node.position) that overrides the auto-layout slot; reads are cache-backed for snapshot stability; viewport persists on settle, not per frame.
KR-011 — No raw window.localStorage; positions/view-state persist only through PersistenceService/UIPreferencesService.
KR-013 — Derive layout/selection state inline or via an external-store subscription, not via useEffect-synced mirrors of props.
Perf — large books must cull off-screen rendering and keep pan/zoom at 60fps; SVG edge count is the usual bottleneck.
A11y — node cards are keyboard-focusable and selectable; the canvas is not a keyboard trap.

iterations_log.label: walking-skeleton + iterations 1-2
architecture_choices: TreeCanvas is a pure VIEW over BookService (KR-020): useOpenBook subscribes to the brain event bus (book:opened, node:*, edge:*) and re-reads the persisted book via useSyncExternalStore — an external-store subscription, not a useEffect-synced mirror (KR-013).

Node mutation lives in BookService (the SSOT): BookService.addNode creates a free-floating node with a deterministic auto-layout slot (autoSlot, KR-023), persists, then emits node:created carrying the kind. The canvas never writes node/edge data itself.

Selection is owned by the canvas (single source of truth, KR-024): local single-select state, broadcast via node:selected{nodeId|null}; node-editor will react to it. Clearing on empty-canvas click emits node:selected null.

Geometry is pure and testable (layout/geometry.ts): resolvePositions auto-lays-out a top-down tree from the choice-edge structure (DFS: y by depth, parent centred over its children's leaf span; linkless/free nodes wrap into a grid below the tree; convergence/cycle-safe via a placed set, KR-080); resolveEdges drops orphaned edges whose endpoints were deleted (KR-021) rather than drawing a line to nowhere. (Originally an autoSlot grid that read stored positions; replaced to fix unreadable sideways parent→child links. Free-node placement went through a bottom row ('all horizontal') and a right column ('one branch') before settling on a wrapping grid below the tree.)
Pan/zoom is local per-session UI state (useViewport) and explicitly NOT persisted/synced here (KR-022); persistence via UIPreferencesService is deferred to iteration 3.

node:created payload extended with `kind` (typed NodeKind) on the brain EventBus — a core domain event emitted by BookService, kept in brain (emitter-owned), consistent with the event-ownership boundary.
deviations_from_plan: Iterations 1 and 2 shipped together as the walking skeleton (faithful § 02 render + live binding + selection + « + Nœud »).

Iteration 3 split: local drag-pan + wheel/control zoom + deterministic auto-layout SHIPPED now; PERSISTING pan/zoom + dragged positions via UIPreferencesService DEFERRED until that service exists (mirrors book-creation iter 3 deferring on CloudSyncService).
New « + Nœud » nodes are seeded as `choix` (a neutral authored screen); retyping happens later in node-editor.
The side panel shown in wireframe § 02 belongs to node-editor (next feature); tree-canvas only emits node:selected to drive it.

test_coverage.unit: BookService.addNode (free-floating, deterministic position, persist-before-emit, unknown-book null); geometry (stored vs auto-layout positions, orphaned-edge drop, label midpoint)
test_coverage.integration: TreeCanvas render (title/count/cards/empty-state placeholder), single-select + node:selected, clear-on-empty-click, « + Nœud » create+select+count via BookService

iterations_log.label: iteration-3
architecture_choices: Built the missing brain UIPreferencesService (KR-025): the single gateway for per-device, non-synced editor view state (pan/zoom, canvas↔outline view-mode, dragged node positions). createBrain wires it over the RAW local store, NOT the CloudSyncService decorator, so this state never enters the cloud queue (KR-022/093/011); its key is the `genliv:ui:book:<id>` namespace (uiPrefsKey), kept out of listBooks.

Reads are served from an in-memory CACHE so getBookPrefs returns a STABLE reference between writes (useSyncExternalStore snapshot stability); each write makes a NEW prefs object and notifies subscribers. New external-store hooks useBookViewMode / useBookNodePositions (KR-013), and useUIPreferences for imperative writes.

Dragged positions are a UI PREFERENCE, not synced node.position: resolvePositions gained an `overrides` param that REPLACES the computed slot for a node (only if still in the book — a deleted node's stale override leaves no ghost, KR-021/023). node.position on the document stays the autoSlot default, unconsulted by the canvas.

useViewport now takes the bookId, seeds the live viewport lazily from the service, and PERSISTS ON SETTLE (drag-release, each zoom step, a centre request) — never every pan frame, so localStorage isn't thrashed at 60fps.

Node drag is a new useNodeDrag hook (window pointer listeners tracked in a ref + unmount cleanup, the BUG-001 pattern): travel past a threshold commits the position via onMove (persisted by the canvas) and consumes the click so a drag-release never selects; a press without travel stays a select. EditorScreen reads/writes the view-mode through the service so the canvas↔outline switch survives a reload.
deviations_from_plan: This iteration also BUILT its blocked dependency (UIPreferencesService) — there is no separate ui-preferences feature; the brain service is infrastructure created by its first consumer (tree-canvas), like SelectionService/SlotRegistry were built within their consuming features.

Orphaned UI prefs: deleting a book leaves its `genliv:ui:book:<id>` entry behind (harmless, keyed by a dead id, never read). A cleanup on book:deleted is deferred (would cross BookService→uiPreferences) — logged as an open question.
jsdom has no PointerEvent, so the drag integration test dispatches coordinate-carrying MouseEvents typed as pointer events (production keeps pointer events, correct in real browsers).

test_coverage.unit: UIPreferencesService (store/read viewport+view-mode+positions, per-book isolation, snapshot-reference stability, position merge, subscribe/unsubscribe, survives-reload, ui: namespace ≠ book key); geometry (a stored override replaces the computed slot; an override for a deleted node leaves no ghost)
test_coverage.integration: TreeCanvas — drag persists a position via UIPreferencesService + overrides the slot (no select on drag), view-mode persists per book, zoom persists per book, view state restored on reload (fresh App over the same store)

iterations_log.label: iteration-4 (robustness at scale)
architecture_choices: OFF-SCREEN CULLING for large books: TreeCanvas measures its surface via a ResizeObserver (imperative DOM measure in a useEffect, KR-013-ok) and renders ONLY the node cards + edges intersecting the visible canvas-space rect (+ a CULL_MARGIN so panning never pops a card in). Pure, testable geometry: viewportRect maps the surface back to canvas space through the translate(x,y) scale(zoom) transform; nodeInView / edgeInView are box/segment-bbox intersection tests. Until the surface is measured (jsdom, first paint) cullRect is null → NO culling (render all), so small/unmeasured cases are unchanged.

Culling is derived inline with useMemo from viewport + measured size (KR-013), never a useEffect-synced mirror; it filters the existing resolvePositions/resolveEdges output, so the layout + orphaned-edge drop (KR-021) are untouched — culling is a pure VIEW filter over them.
deviations_from_plan: Edge-label overlap avoidance is deferred (a minor visual refinement) — the load-bearing iter-4 work is the cull (the SVG edge count + card DOM count are the 60fps bottleneck, now bounded by the viewport). Orphaned-edge guarding (KR-021) was already shipped (resolveEdges drops them).

Culling integration is unit-tested at the pure-geometry level (viewportRect/nodeInView/edgeInView); a full DOM-measured render test is impractical in jsdom (clientWidth is 0, ResizeObserver absent) — the unmeasured path (render-all) is covered by the existing TreeCanvas tests.

test_coverage.unit: geometry cull — viewportRect (pan+zoom mapping), nodeInView (inside/straddle/far/just-past), edgeInView (crossing/inside/outside)
test_coverage.integration: existing TreeCanvas render/select/drag tests still pass (unmeasured surface → no culling, render-all)

resolved_decisions: Editor scope only: « Aperçu du jeu ▷ » is play/book-launch mode (out of scope) — rendered disabled.

Node selection was promoted to a brain SelectionService (single source of truth) during node-editor work: the canvas reads via useSelectedNode and writes via selection.select instead of holding local state, so the editor panel can deselect without desyncing the canvas highlight (KR-024).
Pan/zoom + canvas↔outline view mode are local UI preferences, not synced.

The canvas auto-layout is a deterministic top-down tree derived from the choice-edge structure (sommaire at top; direct children on an evenly-spaced row beneath, parent centred; linkless nodes wrap into a grid below the tree; no 0,0 pileup). BookService.autoSlot (a diagonal cascade by node index) remains the document-level default position but is not consulted for the canvas layout.
« + Nœud » creates a FREE-FLOATING unattached node (kind `choix`), then selects it; attaching to a parent choice is done in choice-linking.
open_questions: Edge-label overlap avoidance for dense graphs (a label-collision pass) — a visual refinement deferred from iter 4.
